spans.s: Khaḍgagrāha (IE 8-3; EI 30), probably the same as Khāḍgika; swordsman; sometimes distinguished from Khaṇḍapāla.
Khaḍgagrāhi-mahāpātra (EI 28, 31), official designation in which Khaḍgagrāhin seems to indicate an officer in charge of swordsmen (as opposed to the clubmen); see Mahāpātra.
Khaḍga-grāhin (EI 28), same as the Khaṇḍāita (originally, swordsmen of the kings of Orissa); cf. Khaḍgagrāha.
Khaḍga-rakṣa (EI 30), same as Khaḍga-grāha; used in place of Aṅgarakṣa and Khaṇḍarakṣa of some records (Ind. Ant., Vol. XVII, p. 11, text line 14); probably, the king's bodyguards.
Khāḍgika (IE 8-3), ‘swordsman’; probably ‘a palace-guard’; mentioned separately from Khaṇḍarakṣa which is also spelt Khaḍgarakṣa.
